h1: The 6 Best Universal Remotes Under $30 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Universal Remotes Under $30: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 universal remotes under $30 compared on device count, code setup, backlight, battery type and and brand coverage.
summary: The GE Rechargeable Backlit remote is the best buy, with a lithium battery you do not swap and four-device control. The GE Backlit with auto code search is the simpler battery-powered alternative, the LOUTOC is for cabinets with DVD, VCR and DVR gear, and the EONCHARM is the right call if you only need a Samsung replacement.
intro: Under $30, the real divide in universal remotes is not features but how they find your TV. Some use a code list you hold a button to enter, some search automatically, and some skip setup because they are a single-brand replacement in disguise. Pick the wrong method and you spend an evening pressing buttons that do nothing.

We ranked six remotes from the listings: how many devices each controls, how setup works, whether the keys are backlit, whether the battery is rechargeable and which brands are named. None are Bluetooth or voice remotes. They use infrared, so they need a clear line to the equipment, and none will pair with a TV stick.

products.name: GE Rechargeable Backlit Universal TV Remote
products.verdict: A rechargeable lithium battery, backlit keys and four-device control with streaming hotkeys.
products.description:
The GE Rechargeable Backlit has a built-in lithium polymer battery that the listing says lasts months, backlit keys, control of up to four devices and streaming app hotkeys.

It ranks first because it removes the two daily annoyances of a living-room remote: dead AAA cells and unlit buttons in the dark. It beats the other GE remotes by dropping disposable batteries, though a built-in battery means a charging cable on the coffee table every few months.

Buy it if you watch evenings in a dim room and own several devices. Skip it if you want a remote with removable batteries that you can swap in seconds.
products.idealFor: Living rooms with several devices and dark viewing.

products.name: GE Backlit Universal Remote Control
products.verdict: A backlit keypad, four-device control and automatic code search on two AAA batteries.
products.description:
The GE Backlit Universal has a backlit keypad, controls four devices, searches codes automatically or accepts direct code entry and runs on two AAA batteries.

It ranks second because it matches the rechargeable model on lighting and device count and swaps in cheap batteries. It loses the top spot because you replace cells every few months, which the rechargeable GE avoids.

Buy it if you want the easiest setup and do not mind AAA cells. Skip it if you want a streaming hotkey layout.

products.idealFor: Dim living rooms where reading keys without a lamp matters.

products.name: GE Universal Remote for Samsung, LG, Roku TV
products.verdict: Four-device control with a Samsung-preprogrammed TV key and a large code library.
products.description:
The GE Universal for Samsung, LG and Roku TV controls four devices, ships with the TV key preprogrammed for Samsung, carries a large code library and runs on two AAA batteries. It names Samsung, LG, Roku TV, Vizio, Sony, Philips and Sharp.

It ranks third because a Samsung TV works on first press, which skips the code hunt, while other brands still need setup. It lacks the backlight of the two GE models above.

Buy it if a Samsung TV is the main screen and you also own a soundbar or box. Skip it if you watch in the dark and need backlit keys.

products.name: Angrox Universal TV Remote Control
products.verdict: Streaming hotkeys for Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+ and Hulu on a no-setup design.
products.description:
The Angrox names seven TV brands, Samsung, Vizio, LG, Hisense, TCL, Philips and Sony, adds hotkeys for Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+ and Hulu, and describes no setup, working by infrared.

It ranks fourth because the hotkeys suit a streaming-first home, but the listing says it is not for TV sticks and offers no device count or backlight. The GE models control more gear.

Buy it if you have one smart TV and no extra boxes. Skip it if you run a soundbar or a cable box, since control of extra devices is not described.

products.idealFor: Streaming-first households with one smart TV.

products.name: LOUTOC Universal TV Remote Control
products.verdict: Eight TV brands plus DVD, Blu-ray, DVR, VCR, soundbar and set-top box, set up by code list.
products.description:
The LOUTOC names eight TV brands, Samsung, LG, Hisense, TCL, Vizio, Sony, Onn and Toshiba, and also handles DVD, Blu-ray, soundbar, streaming player, set-top box, DVR and VCR. Setup means holding SETUP until the red light shows and entering a code.

It ranks fifth because the code-list method is slower than auto search, and it offers no backlight. Its strength is device breadth, which suits a cabinet of older equipment.

Buy it if a VCR or DVR is still in use. Skip it if you dislike entering codes by hand.
products.idealFor: Cabinets with older gear still in use.

products.name: EONCHARM Samsung Replacement Remote
products.verdict: A no-programming Samsung replacement for 2017 through 2024 models.
products.description:
The EONCHARM is a Samsung replacement remote for LCD, LED, HDTV, 3D and Smart models, listed for model years 2017 through 2024, with no programming and a compact easy-grip body.

It ranks last because it is not a true universal remote and controls no other device. Its virtue is zero setup, which suits a lost original.

Buy it if you need a Samsung remote today and nothing else. Skip it if you own more than the TV.
products.idealFor: Samsung owners replacing a lost original.
products.skipIf: You need to control other equipment.

whatMatters.detail: This is the number of devices one remote can control, such as TV, soundbar and streaming box. Four devices cover most living rooms, and one device means a replacement remote. Check the listing for a device count, and count the equipment on your shelf before buying, since a fifth box will not fit.

Setup is how the remote learns your gear. Auto search tries codes for you, a code list needs a printed number, and no-setup remotes are brand specific. Look for the setup steps on the listing, and for a code book in the box. Auto search saves the most time.

A backlit keypad lights up when you press a button, so you can find volume in a dark room. It is a small feature that you use every night. Look for the word backlit on the listing, and note that it adds drain on AAA batteries.

A rechargeable lithium battery lasts months and needs a charging cable, while AAA cells are swapped in seconds. Rechargeable suits remotes that live on a table, and AAA suits families who lose cables. Check which one the listing uses.

These remotes use infrared, so they need a clear line to the device. A cabinet door or a soundbar in the way blocks the signal. Check the listing for infrared wording, and if gear sits behind glass, add an infrared repeater.

faq.q: Will a universal remote work with a streaming stick?
faq.a: Not always. The Angrox listing says it is not for TV sticks, while the GE models control up to four devices that depend on codes. Check the device list on each page before assuming a stick is supported.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Buying a brand-specific replacement as a universal remote. The EONCHARM works only with Samsung TVs from 2017 through 2024, while the GE and LOUTOC models can learn other brands.

faq.q: Is the rechargeable GE worth it over the AAA version?
faq.a: If you hate replacing cells, yes. The rechargeable GE lasts months per the listing and has streaming hotkeys, while the AAA GE offers auto search and swappable batteries.

faq.q: How do I program the LOUTOC?
faq.a: Hold SETUP until the red light stays on, then enter the code for your brand from the list. It is slower than auto search, but it covers older gear like DVD players and VCRs.

faq.q: How do I look after one?
faq.a: Keep it out of direct sun and recharge the GE Rechargeable when keys dim. On the AAA models, remove cells if you store the remote for months to avoid leakage.

faq.q: Do they work through a cabinet door?
faq.a: Infrared needs a clear line, so a closed door blocks it. If your soundbar or box sits behind glass, move the remote closer or open the door.

finalTake: The GE Rechargeable Backlit Universal TV Remote is the best buy under $30 because it fixes dead batteries and dark rooms together. Pick the AAA GE Backlit for auto code search, the GE for Samsung, LG and Roku TV if a Samsung TV leads your setup, and the LOUTOC for older gear. Keep the EONCHARM for a straight Samsung replacement.
